explain.say: Wonderful work! Many Islamic artists used geometry and calligraphy rather than pictures of living things, and patterns like these decorate buildings from Morocco to Iran to India. Wow fact: some medieval patterns in Iran use a clever kind of tiling that mathematicians only described in the 1970s! Challenge: draw a six-pointed star with a compass.

faq.q: Why do Islamic patterns start with a circle?
faq.a: The circle is the simplest perfect shape, and with a compass you can divide it into equal parts. Points on the circle are joined to make stars and polygons that fit together exactly.
A tessellation is a pattern of shapes that fit together with no gaps and no overlaps, repeating across a surface, like tiles on a floor.

faq.q: Why do Islamic patterns use geometry?
faq.a: Many Muslim artists avoided images of people and animals in religious settings, so they developed geometric patterns, plant-like arabesques and beautiful calligraphy. Endless repeating patterns are often seen as a reflection of the infinite.
asks: Why are there no people in Islamic art?
Why are mosques decorated with patterns?

faq.q: Why does the radius fit six times round a circle?
faq.a: Each step makes an equilateral triangle with the centre, whose angle is 60 degrees. Six of them make 360 degrees, a full turn.
asks: Why six points on a circle?

faq.q: Where can I see Islamic geometric art?
faq.a: In places like the Alhambra in Spain, the mosques of Isfahan in Iran, the Taj Mahal in India, and buildings in Morocco, Egypt, Turkey and Uzbekistan.

facts: The radius of a circle can be stepped around its edge exactly six times, because six 60-degree angles make 360 degrees.
The Alhambra in Granada, Spain, was built mainly in the 13th and 14th centuries and is famous for its geometric tilework.
A 2007 study found near-quasicrystal patterns in medieval Islamic tiles, such as at the Darb-i Imam shrine in Isfahan (1453).

quiz.say: You step a compass round a circle using the same width as the radius. How many marks do you get?
quiz.show: The radius fits round the circle…
quiz.why: Each step makes a 60 degree angle at the centre, and six of those make 360 degrees.

wrong.1: Four would need 90 degree steps, which this does not make.
